paper_metadata.title: Quantum-enhanced versus classical Support Vector Machine: An application to stock index forecasting

summary: The paper evaluates a quantum‑enhanced SVM with a quantum kernel estimator on IBM Quantum Experience using 3‑qubit and 2‑qubit circuits for stock index direction prediction. Across 113 rolling experiments (80 training / 20 test samples), classical SVM with an RBF kernel achieves the best performance (>90% balanced accuracy in the separable case), while the quantum kernel SVM performs worse (>80%) and requires about 3 hours 55 minutes per observation—roughly 5.9×10^6 times slower than classical computation.

experiments.description: Quantum-enhanced SVM using a quantum kernel estimator to forecast the future weekly movement direction of the TSX index from lagged TSX, SPX, and CAD returns, compared against classical SVM baselines.

algorithm.variant: quantum-enhanced SVM with quantum kernel estimator (SVM-QKE)
algorithm.optimizer: classical SVM dual optimization (solver not specified)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 3 features mapped to 3 qubits for the TSX experiment; classical returns are embedded into a second-order Pauli-Z evolution circuit and kernel values are estimated via state overlap
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of TSX weekly direction: Direction_TSX(t+1) = f(Return_TSX(t), Return_SPX(t), Return_CAD(t))

problem_instance.description: Forecasting the one-week-ahead direction of the S&P/TSX composite index using lagged returns of TSX, SPX, and CAD

dataset_specification.description: S&P/TSX composite index, S&P 500 index, and USDCAD exchange rate; weekly Wednesday data from 2009-07-08 to 2020-01-22

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: weekly Wednesday sampling; use past returns as features; binary up/down labeling of index movement; limited to small samples due to 5-qubit cloud access
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 113 performance measures from monthly rolling experiments; metrics reported include balanced accuracy, F1-score, precision, and recall

hardware.device_name: IBM Quantum Experience (free public device; specific backend not named)

implementation_details.classical_solver: scikit-learn SVC for classical baseline; classical SVM dual solve for QKE kernel matrix
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: returns computed from market data; weekly Wednesday sampling; rolling-window train/test splits
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: class labels assigned by sign of decision function; metrics averaged over 113 runs
implementation_details.total_execution_time: average 3 hours 55 minutes per observation on cloud quantum computer
implementation_details.quantum_execution_time: average 3 hours 55 minutes per observation on cloud quantum computer

speedup_claims.conditions: cited theory for quantum SVM; assumes coherent quantum data access
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states the practical experiment on real market data does not realize this speedup; quantum-enhanced SVM is reported as 5.9×10^6 times slower in wall-clock time.

speedup_claims.conditions: average per observation on IBM Quantum Experience cloud device
speedup_claims.caveats: Average quantum execution time is 3 hours 55 minutes per observation; range 40 minutes to more than 8 hours.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(log N) claimed for quantum SVM in cited theory
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N) for classical SVM in cited theory
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: local classical computation; quantum version reported as 5.9×10^6 times slower

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: not estimated; theoretical O(log N) scaling cited but not realized due to classical data loading and kernel evaluation overhead
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault‑tolerant quantum computers capable of loading classical financial data coherently (e.g., QRAM) and evaluating quantum kernels at large N; far beyond current 3‑qubit NISQ experiments.
limiting_factors: Classical SVM outperforms quantum-enhanced SVM in accuracy
Extremely slow runtime (≈3h55m per observation on IBM cloud hardware)
Very small dataset and qubit count (3 qubits)
Kernel evaluation requires repeated circuit sampling
Quantum advantage assumptions rely on coherent data access not available here

notes: Hardware type inferred as real_qpu_superconducting because the paper states the experiment ran on an actual IBM Quantum Experience cloud device; specific backend not named.
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; only the feature map structure, repetitions=2, and full entanglement are described.
Section 5 states explicitly that the quantum-enhanced SVM 'does not demonstrate better performance, in terms of both accuracy and computation time, compared to the classical SVM.'
